svg.aria-label: Before early assignment the position is two option legs with the $500 width held against it, $380 net in a margin account. After assignment on the short put it is 100 shares bought at the strike for a $10,000 debit the account must fund or margin, plus the long put, with the loss still capped but the cash already committed.
svg.text: Before: one position, two legs
Short 100 put — obligation
Long 95 put — a right
$5 wide
Credit received at the fill: $120
Held against it: the $500 width, less the credit
$380 net in a margin account; $500 cash in an IRA
Worst case at expiration: $380
No shares, no cash outlay beyond the hold.
After: assigned on the short leg
100 shares, bought at 100
$10,000 debit, settled next day
Long 95 put — still yours
The put still floors the shares at $9,500,
so the capped figure is unchanged: $380.
But the $380 hold is replaced by a $10,000
settlement to fund or margin; short of that,
the broker may liquidate to meet the call.
The notice usually arrives before the open —
the shares are held through the gap regardless.
Hypothetical figures, mechanics only. Fees are not included. Assignment is the holder's decision, made after the close.
